analysis.investment_thesis: CDSL is a financial services / capital markets infrastructure company, and my Magic Formula explicitly excludes financials because the capital structure distorts earnings yield and ROIC calculations. Even waiving that exclusion, the earnings yield is a disqualifying 2.15% (EBIT ₹625 Cr / EV ₹29,098 Cr) — the market has priced the monopoly franchise so richly that there is essentially no value left for new buyers at current prices.
key_strengths: Regulated duopoly with NSDL — near-impenetrable competitive moat as the essential settlement infrastructure for Indian equity markets
Exceptional economics: 51.9% operating margin, 42% ROCE, zero debt, and 27.3% nine-year revenue CAGR — genuinely a world-class business
Asset-light and scalable: incremental accounts (₹1,082 Cr revenue on ₹1,743 Cr equity) drop to the bottom line with minimal marginal cost
key_risks: Earnings yield of 2.15% is the lowest in this batch — at 61× P/E and 42× EV/EBITDA, the stock requires flawless multi-year execution to justify ownership

Revenue is cyclically linked to equity market volumes and new demat account openings — when markets slow, CDSL's transaction fee income contracts sharply (see FY23: revenue flat at ₹555 Cr vs ₹551 Cr in FY22)
Regulatory risk is existential — SEBI controls pricing, fee structures, and market access; any adverse regulatory action would directly compress returns
red_flags: Financial services company — excluded from Magic Formula by design; earnings yield and ROIC comparisons are distorted by the capital-light regulatory structure

FY23 showed the cyclicality clearly: revenue stagnated, operating profit fell from ₹365 Cr to ₹319 Cr, net profit fell from ₹312 Cr to ₹276 Cr — investors are paying 61× for a business with boom-bust characteristics
Promoter holding only 15% — low skin-in-the-game for what is nominally a strategically important infrastructure institution
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By rule, I exclude financial companies from the Magic Formula — capital structure, regulatory capital, and fee-based income make the EBIT/EV and EBIT/capital metrics unreliable. Even setting that aside and running the numbers: EV = ₹29,118 Cr + ₹3 Cr − ₹23 Cr = ₹29,098 Cr; EBIT = ₹625 Cr; earnings yield = 2.15%. That is catastrophically low. CDSL would need to trade at roughly ₹350–400 (from ₹1,393) to reach a 6% earnings yield — a 75% decline. The ROCE of 42% is exceptional, but ROIC quality alone cannot save a stock priced at 42× EV/EBITDA.

The business itself is outstanding — a regulated monopoly with 27% revenue CAGR, zero debt, and 52% operating margins. If CDSL traded at 15–18× EV/EBITDA it would be a strong Magic Formula buy. At 42× I am simply paying for the next decade of growth today, which removes all margin of safety. I would put this on a watchlist and revisit aggressively in any severe market correction that reprices it below 20× EV/EBITDA.
